ports.name: clk_i
ports.functionality: Supplies the rising_edge timing for the entity's synchronous processes; sequences updates to control, counter, reset generation and bus-response registers inside clocked processes.
ports.evidence: Used as rising_edge(clk_i) in processes bus_access, wdt_counter, reset_generator, reset_identifier.

ports.name: rstn_ext_i
ports.functionality: Acts as the asynchronous external reset for the reset_identifier process; when asserted low it forces reset_cause to "00" in the process's reset branch.
ports.evidence: Used in process reset_identifier: if (rstn_ext_i = '0') then reset_cause <= "00".

ports.name: rstn_dbg_i
ports.functionality: When asserted low synchronously (on clk_i) it causes reset_cause to be set to "01" during the reset_identifier process's rising-edge branch.
ports.evidence: In reset_identifier: elsif rising_edge(clk_i) then if (rstn_dbg_i = '0') then reset_cause <= "01".

ports.name: rstn_sys_i
ports.functionality: Provides the system asynchronous reset that clears control, counter, reset flags and bus-response registers in multiple processes when low.
role: sequences clears for ctrl and counters
ports.evidence: Used as process reset in bus_access, wdt_counter, reset_generator: if (rstn_sys_i = '0') then ... end if.

ports.name: bus_req_i
ports.functionality: Provides the bus request bundle; the entity references individual fields (addr, data, stb, rw, etc.) rather than the record as a whole.
ports.evidence: Record fields are referenced (bus_req_i.stb, .rw, .addr, .data); no use of bus_req_i as a whole.

ports.name: bus_req_i.addr
ports.functionality: Carries the 32-bit bus address; bit 2 is tested to select control register writes vs password write behavior in bus_access.
ports.evidence: In bus_access: if (bus_req_i.addr(2) = '0') then ... else ... end if.

ports.name: bus_req_i.data
ports.functionality: Supplies bus write data bits used to update control fields and compared against the reset password; its bits feed ctrl fields on writes and are compared to reset_pwd_c for forced reset.

relationship.evidence: bus_req_i.data compared to reset_pwd_c to decide reset_wdt/reset_force

ports.evidence: Used in bus_access: ctrl fields <= bus_req_i.data(...); if (bus_req_i.data(31 downto 0) = reset_pwd_c) then reset_wdt <= '1'.

ports.name: bus_req_i.ben
ports.functionality: Declared bus byte-enable vector but not referenced in this source; no logic reads or gates on it.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.ben in the source.

ports.name: bus_req_i.stb
ports.functionality: Indicates an active bus request; it directly drives bus_rsp_o.ack and gates the bus_access handling of reads and writes.
ports.evidence: In bus_access: bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb; if (bus_req_i.stb = '1') then ... end if.

ports.name: bus_req_i.rw
ports.functionality: Selects between write and read handling inside bus_access; rw='1' enables write path that updates ctrl fields, otherwise readback assignments occur.
ports.evidence: In bus_access: if (bus_req_i.rw = '1') then (write path) else (readback assignments) end if.

ports.name: bus_req_i.src
ports.functionality: Declared but not referenced in this entity's source; no logic reads or uses this field.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.src in the source.

ports.name: bus_req_i.priv
ports.functionality: Declared but unused in this source; not read or affecting logic here.
ports.evidence: No references to bus_req_i.priv in the source.

ports.name: bus_req_i.debug
ports.functionality: Declared but not used in this entity's logic; no assignments or conditions reference it.
ports.evidence: No uses of bus_req_i.debug appear in the source.

ports.name: bus_req_i.amo
ports.functionality: Declared but not referenced; this design does not use the AMO field.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.amo in the source.

ports.name: bus_req_i.amoop
ports.functionality: Declared but not referenced by the logic in this entity.
ports.evidence: No uses of bus_req_i.amoop in the source.

ports.name: bus_req_i.lock
ports.functionality: Declared but unused in this source; the internal ctrl.lock is different and driven by writes, not by this bus_req lock field here.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.lock in the source.

ports.name: bus_req_i.fence
ports.functionality: Declared but not used in this entity's logic.
ports.evidence: No references to bus_req_i.fence in the source.

ports.name: bus_rsp_o
ports.functionality: Aggregates the response fields (ack, err, data) driven by internal logic; the record is driven in reset and updated on bus transactions inside bus_access, and reaches the entity boundary.
ports.evidence: Assigned as whole in reset and individual fields in bus_access process; bus_rsp_o.ack, .err, .data assigned on clk_i.

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.ack
ports.functionality: Reports an acknowledge for incoming bus requests; on rising clk it captures bus_req_i.stb and is reset by the reset branch assignment to the response record.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb (bus_access process at rising_edge(clk_i)); bus_rsp_o reset in reset branch.

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.err
ports.functionality: Reports an error flag for bus responses; it is driven low on each clock cycle inside bus_access and exported to the bus.
ports.evidence: In bus_access at rising_edge(clk_i): bus_rsp_o.err <= '0'; also reset via bus_rsp_o <= rsp_terminate_c.

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.data
ports.functionality: Carries readback data for bus reads; individual bits and slices are assigned from ctrl fields and reset_cause (on read) and zeroed/reset on reset.
ports.evidence: Readback assignments in bus_access: bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_enable_c) <= ctrl.enable; data(...rcause...)<= reset_cause; timeout slice <= ctrl.timeout.

ports.name: clkgen_en_o
ports.functionality: Reflects the internal ctrl.enable combinationally to the outside world; driven directly from ctrl.enable and exported as an output.
ports.evidence: Concurrent assignment: clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable.

ports.name: clkgen_i
ports.functionality: Provides prescaler clock taps; a specific indexed bit is sampled into prsc_tick (the prescaler tick) driving the watchdog counter logic.
ports.evidence: Assigned: prsc_tick <= clkgen_i(clk_div4096_c) (concurrent bit-index read).

ports.name: rstn_o
ports.functionality: Exports the combined hardware reset output; driven combinatorially as the negation of hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access so external logic sees watchdog- or access-induced resets.
ports.evidence: Concurrent assignment: rstn_o <= not (hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access).

signals.name: ctrl
signals.functionality: Aggregates enable, lock, strict and timeout fields; the code assigns its individual fields in bus_access and the record groups those control bits.
signals.evidence: ctrl_t record declared; fields ctrl.enable/lock/strict/timeout used and assigned in bus_access and reset branches.

signals.name: ctrl.enable
signals.functionality: Holds the watchdog enable; captured on clock from bus write data bit and cleared on system reset. It drives clkgen_en_o, gates counter start and affects reset generation.
signals.evidence: Assigned in bus_access: ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_enable_c); used in cnt_started, hw_rst_* and clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable.

signals.name: ctrl.lock
signals.functionality: Holds the lock flag set by bus write (combined with enable); readback is provided on bus_rsp_o.data. If locked, further writes to control region trigger reset_force.
signals.evidence: bus_access: ctrl.lock <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_lock_c) and ctrl.enable; bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_lock_c) <= ctrl.lock.

signals.name: ctrl.strict
signals.functionality: Holds strict mode flag loaded from bus writes; used in hw_rst_access computation and read back on bus reads.
signals.evidence: Assigned: ctrl.strict <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_strict_c); used in reset_generator hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force; bus readback maps strict bit.

signals.name: ctrl.timeout
signals.functionality: Holds the 24-bit timeout loaded from bus writes (bits 31 downto 8) and reset cleared on reset. It is compared to the counter to produce cnt_timeout and is read back via bus.
signals.evidence: bus_access: ctrl.timeout <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_timeout_msb_c downto ctrl_timeout_lsb_c); cnt_timeout <= '1' when (cnt_started='1') and (cnt = ctrl.timeout).

signals.name: prsc_tick
signals.functionality: Conveys a prescaled clock bit sampled from clkgen_i; used combinationally to drive counter increment gating and to qualify timeout-driven reset generation.
role: sources counter increment and reset gating
signals.evidence: Concurrent assignment: prsc_tick <= clkgen_i(clk_div4096_c); used in wdt_counter and reset_generator.

signals.name: cnt
signals.functionality: Counts up when enabled and prsc_tick-driven; it resets to zero on system reset or when reset_wdt is asserted and increments when cnt_inc indicates a tick.
signals.evidence: wdt_counter: cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1) when cnt_inc = '1'; cnt reset when ctrl.enable='0' or reset_wdt='1'.

signals.name: cnt_started
signals.functionality: Records whether counting is active; set by ctrl.enable and prsc_tick and used to form cnt_inc and to participate in timeout detection.
signals.evidence: wdt_counter: cnt_started <= ctrl.enable and (cnt_started or prsc_tick); cnt_inc <= prsc_tick and cnt_started.

signals.name: cnt_inc
signals.functionality: Is set each clock from prsc_tick and cnt_started to indicate the counter should increment; used as the guard to increment cnt inside the wdt_counter process.
signals.evidence: wdt_counter: cnt_inc <= prsc_tick and cnt_started; later used: if (cnt_inc = '1') then cnt <= cnt + 1.

signals.name: cnt_timeout
signals.functionality: Combinationally indicates when the running counter equals the stored timeout and counting has started; used to trigger a hardware timeout reset when qualified by enable and prsc_tick.
signals.evidence: Concurrent: cnt_timeout <= '1' when (cnt_started = '1') and (cnt = ctrl.timeout) else '0'; used in reset_generator.

signals.name: reset_cause
signals.functionality: Holds a two-bit code that records the most recent reset reason; set to "00" on external reset and updated synchronously to indicate debug, timeout or access resets.
signals.evidence: reset_identifier process sets reset_cause in reset branch and on rising_edge with rstn_dbg_i, hw_rst_timeout, hw_rst_access conditions; read back to bus_rsp_o.data slice.

signals.name: hw_rst_timeout
signals.functionality: Flags that a timeout-induced hardware reset should be produced; captured from ctrl.enable, cnt_timeout and prsc_tick at clock, and used to update reset_cause and the external rstn_o output.
signals.evidence: reset_generator: hw_rst_timeout <= ctrl.enable and cnt_timeout and prsc_tick at rising_edge(clk_i); used in reset_identifier and rstn_o.

signals.name: hw_rst_access
signals.functionality: Flags that an access-caused hardware reset should be produced; captured from ctrl.enable, ctrl.strict and reset_force on clock and used to set reset_cause and the external rstn_o.
signals.evidence: reset_generator: hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force; used in reset_identifier and rstn_o.

signals.name: reset_wdt
signals.functionality: Set on a correct password write to trigger an internal watchdog reset action; it is cleared each cycle and used to clear the counter in the wdt_counter process.
signals.evidence: In bus_access write branch: if (bus_req_i.data(...) = reset_pwd_c) then reset_wdt <= '1'; wdt_counter checks reset_wdt to reset cnt.

signals.name: reset_force
signals.functionality: Set by invalid or disallowed bus writes (attempts to write locked registers or wrong password) and sampled into hw_rst_access calculation; cleared each cycle in bus_access reset or at start of clock handling.
signals.evidence: bus_access sets reset_force <= '1' on disallowed writes; reset_generator computes hw_rst_access using reset_force.
